performShopifyEmbeddedLink: verifyEmbeddedLinkIntent (signed continuation, line 91) then a membership+role check via ctx.supabase (RLS-respecting, merchant_member filtered on ctx.userId + input.merchantAccountId, line 111-127 — refuses any role outside owner/manager, named 'insufficient_role', reproducing shop_insert/shop_update's own RLS rule explicitly rather than relying on it alone) before the admin client is constructed (line 131, used ONLY for the initial global read — detecting a shop owned by another tenant, invisible under RLS). Two more guards run before any write: decideShopAppSwitch (line 143) and decideShopOwnership (line 151, APP-03/Lot 1, reused unmodified). The insert/update themselves use ctx.supabase (RLS-respecting), not admin: root cause of the earlier PostgREST 42501 identified by definitive A/B measurement — INSERT...RETURNING fails the shop_select visibility check (is_shop_member_of) before the AFTER INSERT trigger (shop_seed_memberships, migration 0126) has created the shop_member row in the same transaction; a plain .insert() without .select() never exercises that check and succeeds, leaving the trigger to seed shop_member with the correct role. Proven against real Postgres/RLS (not mocked): tests/rls/shopify-embedded-link-rls.rls.test.ts.

performShopifyAppRelease: role/tenant derived independently from merchant_member via ctx.supabase (RLS-respecting, filtered on ctx.userId, line 99-108) — refuses non-owner as 'insufficient_role' and non-member as 'not_a_member' before the admin client is ever constructed. shop and store_connection are READ via ctx.supabase too (shop_select/store_connection_select policies). The admin client (line 180) is used ONLY for the two tables that have no INSERT/UPDATE policy for authenticated at all — store_connection and store_connection_webhook_token, confirmed by direct catalog read (\d public.store_connection / \d public.store_connection_webhook_token, only a SELECT policy exists on either) — not a choice, the only path these two writes can take. The final shop.shopify_client_id write (line 248) uses ctx.supabase (RLS-respecting, shop_update policy permits owner/manager — the applicative gate above is already stricter, owner only), same discipline as embedded-link-write.ts. Every admin write is a compare-and-set scoped by id + merchant_account_id (+ status/old-value predicates) — never a bare id. Proven against real Postgres/RLS (not mocked), including concurrent-call and cross-tenant/role refusal: tests/rls/shopify-app-release.rls.test.ts.
